target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The diagnostic layer (`detectToolCallShapedText`) correctly classifies these JSON shapes, but the promotion layer (`parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks`) only recognizes bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats — leaving a gap where the system can see the tool call but cannot act on it.

Additionally, two related gaps discovered during review:

- **Stream leakage**: The stream normalizer's buffer-state logic only checked bracket, XML, and Harmony prefixes. A provider streaming `{"name":"read","arguments":...}` would emit that JSON as visible text before the final `done` event promotes it, violating the stream scrubbing invariant.
- **Multi-call truncation**: The JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, silently dropping every subsequent entry in a multi-tool wrapper response.

This affects providers that route through `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` (Ollama, LM Studio, xAI) when the underlying model embeds tool calls in the assistant content as JSON objects.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix operates in two layers of the `tool-call-repair` package:

**1. Payload parser** (`payload.ts`): `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` recognizes 4 JSON tool-call shapes and now returns an array — an OpenAI-style `tool_calls` wrapper with multiple entries emits one block per valid entry instead of silently truncating to the first.

**2. Stream normalizer** (`stream-normalizer.ts`): Adds `couldStillBeJsonToolCall` and `hasJsonToolCallPrefix` so the buffer-state engine treats JSON-format stream text as buffered tool-call candidates instead of flushing it as visible text. Updated `getPlainTextToolCallBufferState` and `stripCompleteSerializedToolCallPrefix` to handle standalone JSON objects.

Existing safety gates are preserved: `allowedToolNames` whitelist filtering and the standalone-only invariant (entire text must be consumed by tool-call blocks — no mixed prose).

This is the correct ownership boundary because `tool-call-repair` is the canonical location for text-to-tool-call promotion, and all providers using `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` automatically benefit.

## User Impact

Affected: users routing tool-calling agents through local/proxy providers (Ollama, LM Studio, xAI) with models that serialize tool calls as JSON text in `content` rather than through native `tool_calls` fields (observed with Qwen family models).

After fix: JSON-embedded tool calls are buffered during streaming (preventing text leakage), all entries in multi-call wrappers are promoted (not just the first), and tool calls are correctly parsed and promoted into executable tool calls.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload` — 34 passed (32 existing + 2 new: multi-call wrapper parsing and stripping)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean
- `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet <changed-files>` — clean
- `oxfmt --check <changed-files>` — clean
- `pnpm build` — passed (all packages built successfully)
- CI: all checks passing on commit `c5c0853fa1`

Behavior addressed:
1. JSON-format tool-call text is buffered during streaming via `couldStillBeJsonToolCall` / `hasJsonToolCallPrefix` instead of leaking as visible text
2. Every entry in an OpenAI-style `tool_calls` wrapper is promoted (not just the first)
3. JSON-format plain-text tool calls are promoted to executable tool calls through the same path as bracket/XML/Harmony formats

Environment: Linux dev checkout, Node 22.

ClawSweeper rank-up moves addressed in revision `c5c0853fa1`:
- [P1] JSON-aware stream buffering — `couldStillBeJsonToolCall` + `hasJsonToolCallPrefix` in `stream-normalizer.ts`
- [P2] Multi-call `tool_calls` promotion — `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` now iterates all entries and returns `{name, arguments}[]`

Commands run after this patch:
```
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
pnpm format:check packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
pnpm build
```

Evidence after fix: All 34 tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format, and build all clean.

What was not tested: Live end-to-end reproduction with a real Ollama instance and Qwen model — no local Ollama setup available. The stream-buffering gap is verified at the source level: `couldStillBeJsonToolCall` gates buffering with the same JSON key-set the diagnostic layer uses, and the prefix recognition matches the shapes already classified by `classifyJsonValue`.
